deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding pages build a combinatorial ('Lego') presentation of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower. They count vertices and arrows (twists τ, 'gommages' γ) of a big diagram in modular dimension ≤ 2. This page turns to the special points of the 2-dimensional modular space M_{0,5}. These are configurations of 5 marked points K on Σ = P^1 (over C, or an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0) whose automorphism group G = Aut(Σ,K) is nontrivial. Equivalently, they are the points with nontrivial stabiliser for the action of S_5, or the fixed points of torsion elements of the mapping class group Γ_{0,[5]} on Teichmüller space, i.e. the orbifold points of M_{0,[5]}. The left margin points to exactly this: 'pt fixe de l'opération du groupe de Teichm.'

Method. Take g in G of maximal order ν. A finite-order automorphism of P^1 (order prime to the characteristic) has exactly two fixed points, and <g> ≅ μ_ν acts freely on the complement. Hence K = K^g ⊔ (free orbits of size ν), with |K^g| ≤ 2. So 5 = a + bν with a ≤ 2, which gives 2 ≤ ν ≤ 5.

(1) ν=5, a=0. K is one orbit; we may take K = μ_5 (regular pentagon on the equator). It is unique up to isomorphism, with Aut = D_5. In groupoid terms it is a 'principal homogeneous / pentagon structure' on I.
(2) ν=4, a=1. K = μ_4 ∪ {0} (square pyramid), Aut = Z/4 ≅ μ_4. The groupoid of such configurations is equivalent to that of oriented squares.
(3) ν=3, a=2. K = μ_3 ∪ {0,∞} (triangular bipyramid), Aut = D_3. The groupoid is equivalent to Ens(3), the 3-element sets. Given J, one recovers Σ_J with J ∪ P_J; over C the two poles correspond bijectively to the two orientations of J.
(4) ν=2 (next page). K = {0, ±1, ±√λ}. This is a 1-parameter family with parameter ρ = λ + 1/λ, which Grothendieck notes has 'moduli' and is less interesting. Its degenerations recover the square and the tetrahedral/octahedral configurations.

The next page then treats anti-holomorphic involutions, i.e. real structures, classified by |K^σ| ∈ {1,3,5}.

The purpose is to identify the torsion and special loci of M_{0,5}. These correspond to the finite-order relations (pentagon of order 5, etc.) in the presentation of Γ_{0,5} being worked out on the neighbouring pages.
errors: The key lemma (every finite-order automorphism has exactly two fixed points and acts freely elsewhere) needs the order to be prime to the characteristic. Grothendieck restricts to characteristic 0 and adds a marginal doubt about characteristic 2 and 3, which is justified. In characteristic p there are extra special configurations. For example, in characteristic 5 the set K = F_5 is stable under the affine group AGL(1,5) of order 20.
No real errors in characteristic 0. The groups D_5, Z/4 and D_3 and the case analysis are correct. The ν=2 family (next page) indeed contains points with larger symmetry, as he notes.

ideas.what: Classification of 5-point configurations on P^1 with nontrivial automorphism group: pentagon (D_5), square pyramid (C_4), triangular bipyramid (D_3), plus a 1-parameter C_2 family.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold/special loci of M_{0,5} (M_{0,[5]}); torsion of the genus-0 mapping class group Γ_{0,[5]}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (finite subgroups of PGL_2); in the GT context L. Schneps ('special loci', ~2003) and B. Collas (torsion in Γ_{0,n} and GT action, ~2012)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and modular dimensions ≤2, but an explicit list of this kind is not known to me there

ideas.what: Describing each special locus as a groupoid equivalent to a combinatorial groupoid (pentagons, oriented squares, Ens(3)).
ideas.modern_name: Residual gerbes / stack inertia at special points; anabelian-style combinatorial models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in later work on stack inertia (Collas, Collas–Maugeais)

ideas.what: Classification of real structures (antiholomorphic involutions) preserving K by |K^σ| ∈ {1,3,5}.
ideas.modern_name: Real points / real components of M_{0,5}

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly ties the special (torsion) points of M_{0,5} to his combinatorial presentation of the Teichmüller tower. The order-5 pentagon point would naturally correspond to the pentagon relation. This anticipates the later program of using torsion and special loci to constrain GT. That program was later carried out (Schneps; Nakamura–Schneps; Collas), so it is not genuinely missed, but this is early documentary evidence of Grothendieck's own intent.
missed.quote: pt fixe de l'opération du groupe de Teichm.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only: it shows the special-loci approach to GT originates in Grothendieck's 1983 notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The classification is classical and correct. Its interest is historical: Grothendieck was studying the torsion and special loci of M_{0,5} alongside his Lego presentation, a direction later developed by Schneps and Collas.
transcription_corrections: The line before 'celle Ens(3)' plausibly reads 'combinatoires i.e. celle Ens(3) des ens. J de card 3' rather than a continuation about equilateral triangles.
In case (3), the stray '$\Sigma$' before 'card $K^g=2$' is a struck-out symbol.
The marginal notes 'pyramide carrée' and 'bipyramide' label cases (2) and (3) respectively; the 'pentagone' note refers to case (1).
